newsitem.title: BARBADOS: CRICKET-SRI LANKA REPLACE INJURED PAIR.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA REPLACE INJURED PAIR.

text.p: Injury-hit Sri Lanka are flying two replacement players to the Caribbean after losing the first test to West Indies inside three days in St John's, Antigua, on Sunday.
All-rounder Ruwan Kalpage and left-handed batsman Naveed Nawaz were expected in Antigua on Monday to join the battered Sri Lankan squad which has been reduced to 12 fit players.

Fast bowler Nuwan Zoysa, who missed the first match of the two-test series with a stress fracture of the lower back, has already returned home and will be joined by middle order batsman Hashan Tillekeratne, who was due to leave St John's on Monday.
Tillekeratne fractured his right forearm after being struck by a delivery from fast bowler Courtney Walsh on the opening day of the test, which West Indies won by six wickets.
He retired hurt on one and after his hand was placed in a cast, did not resume his innings nor bat in the second innings.

Batsman Marvan Atapattu, who was ruled out of the test with a fractured index finger, is staying in the Caribbean but remains doubtful for the second test starting in Kingstown, St Vincent, on Friday.
West Indies will be without Shivnarine Chanderpaul for the final test.

The left-hander, who missed the one-off limited overs international in Port of Spain and the first test, has been ordered to rest after seeing two doctors in Barbados at the weekend about his injured neck.
West Indies Cricket Board secretary Andrew Sealy said Chanderpaul has muscle spasms in the neck and has returned to his home in Guyana.
